register.name: 2026 Supplementary Budget
register.detail: Department of Treasury · supplementary budget speech of 1 September 2026 · total 2026 expenditure K32,245 million · K1,330 million added to revenue and expenditure · deficit K1,608 million, 1.0% of GDP
register.note: The speech expects the debt to GDP ratio to fall to under 45%, and cites up to K300 million in concessional World Bank financing for El Niño if a national emergency is declared
register.text: The supplementary budget raises Papua New Guinea’s 2026 expenditure to a record K32,245 million while the deficit falls to 1.0% of GDP. It carries the public services behind the seven standards, with large increases in support for teachers and health workers cited in the speech.

register.name: Rural Service Delivery Project Phase 2 (RSDP-2)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA credit) · approval announced 10 August 2026 · P508616 · appraisal document of 17 July 2026 · subnational governments add 15% in counterpart funds
register.note: More than one million people, about 300,000 of them in remote areas; over 39,000 job opportunities expected from community works
register.text: An IDA credit for at least 800 community-chosen investments in clean water, sanitation, health facilities, classrooms, rural roads, electricity and livelihood activities, with stronger local planning. It serves the water, health, education, energy and livelihood standards in the villages furthest from services.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility and Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 22 March 2023 · 260% of quota · sixth reviews completed 8 June 2026 · SDR 60.53 million (about US$82 million) released
register.note: About SDR 742.23 million (about US$1,012 million) disbursed under IMF-supported programmes by June 2026
register.text: IMF arrangements that support Papua New Guinea’s reforms to raise revenue, rationalise spending, restore the convertibility of the kina and strengthen governance. The Board urged fiscal space for social and capital spending; the arrangements finance the balance of payments and the budget as a whole.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 11 December 2024 · 75% of quota · 24 months · third review completed 8 June 2026 · SDR 59.22 million (about US$81 million) released
register.note: Three RSF reform measures implemented by the third review
register.text: Longer-term IMF financing that runs alongside the ECF and EFF arrangements and rewards reforms for resilience. It finances the budget as a whole, in a nation exposed to natural disasters and unstable utilities.

register.name: Budget support for reforms to boost revenue
register.detail: World Bank · Board approval announced 15 December 2025 · includes a US$50 million Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, the first for Papua New Guinea
register.note: Reforms include a new Income Tax Bill with a tax on capital gains, a stronger dividend policy for state-owned enterprises and the Biosecurity Bill 2025
register.text: World Bank budget support for reforms that raise tax revenue and returns from state-owned enterprises and ease trade, with contingent finance ready for disasters. It finances the public budget as a whole and protects spending on the seven standards when disaster strikes.

register.name: REDD-plus results-based payments, 2014–2016 (FP273)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved at the 42nd Board meeting, held in Port Moresby, 30 June to 3 July 2025 · FAO · pilot programme for results-based payments
register.note: Agroforestry, sustainable fuelwood and charcoal production, and community pole and timber plantations
register.text: A Green Climate Fund payment for forest results Papua New Guinea achieved in 2014–2016, invested through FAO in sustainable forest management with benefit sharing for communities. It serves the livelihood and energy standards through agroforestry and sustainable fuelwood.

register.name: National Energy Access Transformation Project
register.note: pv magazine reports a $204 million initiative, with a $4.2 million grant from the Global Partnership for Results-Based Approaches
register.text: A World Bank project for grid extension and off-grid power for homes without electricity. It serves the energy standard, where fewer than half of Papua New Guineans have electricity.

register.name: Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Security and Resilience Improvement Project
register.detail: ADB · 25 February 2026 · $30M regular and $30.9M concessional ordinary capital resources loans · $1.5M technical assistance grant · $3M from the Government · Water PNG Limited
register.note: More than 160,000 people in Port Moresby and Vanimo; ADB’s first loan to the water sector in more than 25 years
register.text: ADB loans to rehabilitate the Mount Eriama water treatment plant and the Waigani sewage ponds in Port Moresby, cut non-revenue water and build a new water system with metered household connections in Vanimo, which has no reticulated supply. It serves the water and shelter standards, including in settlements.

register.name: Sustainable Energy Sector Development Program
register.detail: ADB · approval announced 16 December 2025 · $100M loan and a $10M grant from the Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism · PNG Power Limited
register.note: One of three ADB approvals totalling $275 million announced the same day
register.text: ADB financing to make low-carbon electricity supply adequate, restore the sustainability of the power sector, improve the performance of PNG Power Limited and draw in private investment. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach.
by: Japan Fund for the Joint Crediting Mechanism

register.name: Improving Financial Access Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: ADB · policy-based loan · approval announced 16 December 2025 · Subprogram 2 to continue the reforms
register.text: An ADB policy-based loan that strengthens the rules and institutions for payments, remittances, credit and capital, to widen access to finance for households and businesses. It supports the budget and the livelihood standard.

register.name: Australian development assistance, 2026–27
register.detail: Australian Government · total ODA budget estimate 2026–27 · bilateral program A$500 million · an estimated A$707 million in 2025–26
register.note: Australia reports helping deliver solar power to more than 21,000 homes
register.text: Australia’s official development assistance to Papua New Guinea for 2026–27, with A$500 million in the bilateral program for health and nutrition, education and economic growth. It serves several of the seven standards, among them energy through household solar.

register.name: Improvement of Facilities and Training Equipment of National Fisheries College
register.detail: Government of Japan, JICA grant aid · grant agreement signed in Port Moresby 20 June 2025 · up to ¥3,255 million
register.note: A new jetty, a seawall, training facilities for fishing gear and maritime safety, and a training vessel
register.text: A Japanese grant to rebuild the waterfront and training equipment of the National Fisheries College. It trains the people who work Papua New Guinea’s fisheries, serving the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Budget support loan, 2024
register.detail: Commonwealth of Australia · signed 12 December 2024 · 20 years · interest at the Australian Government cost of borrowing
register.note: Australia reports A$3.16 billion in budget support loans to Papua New Guinea since 2019, not counted as aid
register.text: An Australian loan to help cover the financing shortfall of Papua New Guinea’s 2024 Budget and support reforms under its IMF programme. It finances the public budget as a whole.

enterprises.heading: Already working in Papua New Guinea.

items.name: Homes Purse Clean Energy
items.text: A small business in Port Moresby that has taken to market a clean fuel for domestic use made from local waste, an affordable alternative to collecting firewood for cooking, given a special commendation in the 2026 Innovation PNG Awards.

items.name: Bayside Cooperative Society
items.text: A community-driven cooperative on Sideia Island, Milne Bay, that supplies fresh fish to local markets, schools and shops, supported by the UNDP Gutpela Solwara, Gutpela Bisnis project.

items.name: Refah Fisheries Suppliers
items.text: A woman-led fisheries business in Gamadoudou ward, near Alotau, that buys fish from trained local fishers for buyers in town, enforces responsible fishing practices and is adding solar-powered refrigeration and ice-making.

items.name: Women’s Micro Bank (Mama Bank)
items.text: The only women-focused financial institution in Papua New Guinea, which reaches rural women through Mama Access Points and, with a UNCDF portfolio guarantee, had made 293 loans worth $265,000 to women-owned and women-led enterprises by December 2024.

items.name: Highland Organic Agriculture Cooperative
items.text: A Fairtrade-certified cooperative of coffee farmers whose members trained in 2025 to record farm geolocation data, which the European Union’s deforestation rules require of coffee sold there.

items.name: Club 3000 Farmers Cooperative Society
items.text: A Fairtrade-certified cooperative of cocoa farmers whose members trained in 2025 to record farm geolocation data, keeping their cocoa open to European Union markets.
